question: What did the SEC charge ICAP Securities USA LLC with?
answer_given: The SEC charged ICAP Securities USA LLC with fraud for engaging in deceptive broking activity and making material misrepresentations to customers concerning its trading activities [SEC.gov _ SEC Charges U.S. Subsidiary of World’s Largest Inter-Dealer Broker for Displaying Fictitious Trades and Misleading Customers.pdf, page 1].

question: How much did ICAP agree to pay to settle the SEC's charges?
answer_given: ICAP agreed to pay $25 million in disgorgement and penalties to settle the SEC's charges [SEC.gov _ SEC Charges U.S. Subsidiary of World’s Largest Inter-Dealer Broker for Displaying Fictitious Trades and Misleading Customers.pdf, page 2]. This total consists of $1 million in disgorgement and $24 million in penalties [SEC.gov _ SEC Charges U.S. Subsidiary of World’s Largest Inter-Dealer Broker for Displaying Fictitious Trades and Misleading Customers.pdf, page 3].

question: How many ICAP brokers did the SEC charge with aiding and abetting the firm's fraudulent conduct?
answer_given: The SEC charged five ICAP brokers with aiding and abetting the firm’s fraudulent conduct [SEC.gov _ SEC Charges U.S. Subsidiary of World’s Largest Inter-Dealer Broker for Displaying Fictitious Trades and Misleading Customers.pdf, page 2].

question: Why were the two senior executives charged?
answer_given: The two senior executives were charged for failing reasonably to supervise the brokers [SEC.gov _ SEC Charges U.S. Subsidiary of World’s Largest Inter-Dealer Broker for Displaying Fictitious Trades and Misleading Customers.pdf, page 2].

question: What were the fictitious flash trades also known as?
answer_given: The fictitious flash trades were also known as "bird" trades [SEC.gov _ SEC Charges U.S. Subsidiary of World’s Largest Inter-Dealer Broker for Displaying Fictitious Trades and Misleading Customers.pdf, page 1].

question: Between which dates did ICAP's brokers display thousands of fictitious flash trades?
answer_given: ICAP’s UST brokers displayed thousands of fictitious flash trades between December 2004 and December 2005 [SEC.gov _ SEC Charges U.S. Subsidiary of World’s Largest Inter-Dealer Broker for Displaying Fictitious Trades and Misleading Customers.pdf, page 2].

question: Who was the former President of ICAP North America charged by the SEC?
answer_given: Ronald A. Purpora was the former President of ICAP North America charged by the SEC [SEC.gov _ SEC Charges U.S. Subsidiary of World’s Largest Inter-Dealer Broker for Displaying Fictitious Trades and Misleading Customers.pdf, page 2].

question: How much was the penalty for each broker other than Hoffman?
answer_given: Each broker other than Hoffman has agreed to pay a $100,000 penalty [SEC.gov _ SEC Charges U.S. Subsidiary of World’s Largest Inter-Dealer Broker for Displaying Fictitious Trades and Misleading Customers.pdf, page 4].

question: Which sections of the securities laws did the SEC find ICAP willfully violated?
answer_given: The SEC found that ICAP willfully violated Section 17(a)(2) and 17(a)(3) of the Securities Act of 1933, and Section 15C of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and 17 CFR Parts 404 and 405 [SEC.gov _ SEC Charges U.S. Subsidiary of World’s Largest Inter-Dealer Broker for Displaying Fictitious Trades and Misleading Customers.pdf, page 3].

question: How much of the Connecticut state pension fund did the then-Connecticut Treasurer invest with Thayer IV in November 1998?
answer_given: The Connecticut Treasurer increased the investment in Thayer IV to $75 million [SEC.gov _ Thayer Capital Partners, TC Equity Partners IV, L.L.C., TC Management Partners IV, L.L.C., and Frederic V. Malek.pdf, page 3].

question: What were the total payments made to the Treasurer's Associate?
answer_given: The Treasurer's Associate received total payments of $374,500 [SEC.gov _ Thayer Capital Partners, TC Equity Partners IV, L.L.C., TC Management Partners IV, L.L.C., and Frederic V. Malek.pdf, page 3].

question: What percentage of the amount Connecticut invested was Thayer to pay the Treasurer's Associate's consulting firm?
answer_given: Thayer was to pay the Treasurer's Associate's consulting firm 0.7% of the amount Connecticut invested [SEC.gov _ Thayer Capital Partners, TC Equity Partners IV, L.L.C., TC Management Partners IV, L.L.C., and Frederic V. Malek.pdf, page 3].

question: What civil money penalty was Thayer ordered to pay?
answer_given: Thayer was ordered to pay a civil money penalty in the amount of $150,000 [SEC.gov _ Thayer Capital Partners, TC Equity Partners IV, L.L.C., TC Management Partners IV, L.L.C., and Frederic V. Malek.pdf, page 5].

question: What civil money penalty was Frederic V. Malek ordered to pay?
answer_given: Frederic V. Malek was ordered to pay a civil money penalty in the amount of $100,000 [SEC.gov _ Thayer Capital Partners, TC Equity Partners IV, L.L.C., TC Management Partners IV, L.L.C., and Frederic V. Malek.pdf, page 5].

question: What did the respondents fail to disclose to the Connecticut pension funds?
answer_given: Respondents failed to disclose material facts to the Connecticut pension funds, specifically that at the request of the Connecticut Treasurer, the Treasurer's Associate—who had no previous involvement with the proposed investment and did no meaningful work—was paid a fee in connection with the Treasurer's investment of state pension funds with Thayer IV [SEC.gov _ Thayer Capital Partners, TC Equity Partners IV, L.L.C., TC Management Partners IV, L.L.C., and Frederic V. Malek.pdf, pages 2, 4].

question: How much money does Thayer, the Washington, DC private equity firm, manage in funds?
answer_given: Thayer manages funds totaling over $1.2 billion [SEC.gov _ Thayer Capital Partners, TC Equity Partners IV, L.L.C., TC Management Partners IV, L.L.C., and Frederic V. Malek.pdf, page 2].

question: To what amount was the Connecticut pension funds' investment in Thayer IV reduced after the new Treasurer took office?
answer_given: The Connecticut pension funds' investment in Thayer IV was reduced from $75 million to $53.5 million [SEC.gov _ Thayer Capital Partners, TC Equity Partners IV, L.L.C., TC Management Partners IV, L.L.C., and Frederic V. Malek.pdf, page 3].
